headings.text: What your wallet holds. What it is owed.

Paste an address. Your browser reads every Robinhood Stock Token it holds, straight from the chain, and states what each declared dividend would owe it. No signature, no account, nothing sent to exdate.
Read in your browser, straight from Robinhood Chain’s public node. No signature. exdate has no server, so the address goes nowhere else.

headings.text: How much warning the chain gives
How long after the issuer’s own date
The issuer says paid. The chain says nothing.
What can be measured, and what stops the rest

fold: How much warning the chain gives

A multiplier change is published on chain before it takes effect. Of the 12 changes seen so far, 11 came 9 to 10 minutes ahead and one, CRWD, came 74 minutes ahead. Nothing is emitted when the change actually takes effect, so the announcement is the only signal there is.

mobile.title: Creations and redemptions — exdate
fold: Read from the chain, no oracle involved

A Stock Token is minted when an authorised participant deposits the underlying and burned when they redeem it. Minting is a transfer from the zero address, redeeming a transfer to it, so the difference is exact: it is the same signal an ETF publishes daily as net flow, and it says whether the wrapper is growing. Nobody publishes it for these tokens — the issuer’s own feed carries gross turnover, with no sign and no history.

3203 creations and 513 redemptions in this window, which runs from 4 September at 06:20 to 5 September at 05:20 UTC. Amounts are tokens; the shares they represent are these times each token’s multiplier.

mobile.title: Oracle gap — exdate

headings.text: What it trades at, and what the oracle says.
Every token that trades and has a feed
And 41 that trade with no oracle at all
Does the gap widen when the feed freezes?

fold: What it trades at, and what the oracle says.

A lending market liquidates against the Chainlink price. That feed runs 24/5 and holds its last answer outside market hours; the chain never stops trading. The distance between the two is the risk a curator carries, and it is widest exactly when the feed is stalest. At this reading the median feed was 975 minutes old and the median token traded 39 basis points from it.

mobile.title: API reference — exdate
fold: Every example below is a real response, captured from the indexer running against Robinhood Chain mainnet on 2026-09-02. Nothing here is illustrative: if a field is null in an example, that is what the chain said.

Base URL: https://api.exdate.me, or wherever you run the indexer yourself — http://localhost:42069 under pnpm dev, or the box deploy/install-api.sh sets up (see Hosting in the README). The public instance is one small machine with no availability commitment. :chain accepts the key (robinhood) or the id (4663).
every bigint is a decimal string — "1005101770003214918", never a JS number;
anything exdate has not observed is null — never 0, never a default, never an absent key.

A third rule governs prices: Chainlink's Robinhood feeds publish Token Price = Underlying Equity Price × Multiplier. The multiplier is already in the answer. Every response that carries a price says so in answerIncludesMultiplier / includesMultiplier.

Every route but /v1/health is counted. Without a key a caller shares an anonymous quota per client address (60 requests a minute by default); with one, the quota the operator attached to it. The key travels as Authorization: Bearer <key> or X-Api-Key: <key>, and three headers come back on every answer: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (a Unix timestamp). mobile.title: SDK — exdate
fold: Typed client and webhook verifier for the exdate API — the corporate-action layer for Robinhood Chain Stock Tokens.

Nothing is computed in this package. Every number it returns traces back to a log, an ERC-8056 view call or the issuer's own feed, and the two API rules hold throughout: every bigint is a decimal string, and anything exdate has not observed is null — never 0, never absent.
Until the package is on npm, add it from the workspace ("@exdate/sdk": "workspace:*") or from a checkout. It depends on @exdate/core only; installing it never pulls in the server.
